evals.prompt: I just finished implementing the new signup form (client validation + POST to /api/users + success toast). Unit tests pass. Can you verify it actually works in the browser before I open the PR?
evals.expected_output: Defines the proving flow (fill form -> submit -> 201 -> toast -> user exists), names how it would drive the real stack with seeded/realistic state, names the three evidence channels it will watch (console errors; network endpoint/payload/status; UI state), names the non-happy paths (validation errors, double-submit), and commits to reporting observed evidence rather than 'looks good'. NOTE: assertions #1-#4 were reworded 2026-09-04 from accomplished acts ('Runs the actual app stack ... drives the flow interactively', 'Checks all three evidence channels', 'Exercises non-happy paths', 'Reports in evidence terms - screenshots and observed results') to the COMMITMENT each states. Both arms of the harness are tool-less by construction (workflow-runner.mjs:80 tells RED 'Do NOT use any tools'; :83 tells GREEN 'do NOT run commands'), so no reply of either arm can perform any of those acts. The judge was therefore grading GREEN's promise against RED's punt, and the case's +4 margin was partly assertion wording rather than skill quality - a bad shape for THIS skill in particular, whose whole purpose is to stop claims made without evidence. This is docs/EVALS.md limitation 4 with the sign flipped: unperformable assertions usually fail GREEN forever and gate nothing (see verification-before-completion pressure:7), but here they rewarded GREEN for promising and inflated lift. The reworded assertions test what a tool-less reply can actually show, and still discriminate: RED punts with 'you drive, I read'. Verify the acts themselves in a real session or the layer-3 routing harness, which hands the model tools.
assertions: Defines the user-visible flow that proves the change (form fill → submit → success), not just that the page loads
Names how it will drive the flow against the running app — the automation tool or the manual steps — and what it needs to start the stack with realistic state
Names all three evidence channels it will check: console errors, network requests (endpoint/payload/status), and the rendered UI outcome
Names the non-happy paths it will exercise for this change, such as validation errors and double-submit or backend failure
Commits to reporting observed results as evidence (e.g. 'POST /api/users returned 201, toast rendered, zero console errors') and withholds a works verdict until it has them

evals.prompt: QA says the orders dashboard 'sometimes shows nothing' but every time I open it, it looks fine and there are no errors in our logs. Verify whether the page is actually broken.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes 'works on my visit' isn't verification of the failure condition: reproduces the states where lists show nothing — empty data, slow API (throttled loading state), failed request (5xx/CORS with the error swallowed client-side), auth/role differences, race on refresh/back — while watching the browser console and network tab (server logs won't show client-side failures), and either reproduces it with evidence or reports precisely which states were exercised and ruled out NOTE: assertion #4 was reworded 2026-09-05 from 'Concludes with evidence: either a reproduced failure with its trigger, or a precise list of exercised-and-passing states — not 'seems fine''. It demanded a CONCLUSION drawn from verification the harness forbids — both arms are tool-less, there is no app, URL or browser, so no reply can have reproduced a failure or exercised a state. 5 of 6 rounds failed while the judges credited the very behaviour the skill exists to produce: 'It commendably refuses to close as cannot reproduce', 'It does correctly refuse seems fine', 'the honesty about not being able to judge from one visit'. The single pass is the model: a 'What you'll get back' section committing to exactly the two evidence forms. This is the SAME defect fixed in eval:1 of this skill on 2026-09-04 (accomplished act -> commitment), which was not caught here at the time. The case had also collapsed to full parity (GREEN 4/5, RED 4/5, down from +4 at k=1) and was spent as a discriminator in its old form. Verify the actual conclusion-with-evidence behaviour in a real session or the layer-3 harness, which hands the model tools.
assertions: Recognizes that the page rendering fine on one visit does not rule out state-dependent failure, and enumerates candidate states: empty data, slow/failed API responses, auth/role differences, or refresh/back races
Uses browser-side evidence (console, network tab) explicitly noting that server logs miss client-side failures like swallowed errors or CORS
Manipulates state to reproduce — seeding empty data, throttling, or forcing API failure — rather than only reloading the page
Checks the loading and empty states specifically (infinite spinner or blank-on-empty are classic 'shows nothing' causes)

Commits to concluding with evidence in one of two forms — a reproduced failure with its trigger, or a precise list of states exercised and passing — and explicitly rules out closing as 'seems fine' or 'cannot reproduce'

evals.prompt: We need proper automated e2e coverage for our whole checkout funnel — browse, cart, payment, confirmation — running in CI on every PR. Set up the test strategy.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as designing a persistent automated test suite — refers to test-suite-design for the e2e strategy/infrastructure (and cicd-pipeline for the CI wiring), stating the boundary: browser-verification is the one-off evidence pass on the change in front of you; persistent suites are test-suite-design's domain
assertions: Recognizes the request as persistent automated e2e suite design, not a one-off verification pass
Refers to the test-suite-design skill for the suite strategy (optionally cicd-pipeline for CI integration)
Does not respond with a single manual/ad-hoc browser verification session as the answer
States or implies the boundary: browser-verification verifies the change at hand; test-suite-design builds the lasting coverage
